title: Model Routing & Provider Selection in the ZES AI Gateway
excerpt: How to route requests across OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, Azure, and AWS Bedrock — with cost, latency, and capability-based rules.
content:
# Model Routing & Provider Selection in the ZES AI Gateway

The ZES AI gateway aggregates 40+ upstream AI providers — OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, Azure, AWS Bedrock, and more — behind a single OpenAI-compatible API. But not every request should hit your most capable (and most expensive) model. Smart routing is how you control spend and latency without degrading quality.

## Why route by model

Different tasks need different models:

- Classification, extraction, and short summarization → smaller, cheaper models
- Complex reasoning, coding, and creative writing → flagship models
- High-volume, latency-sensitive traffic → fast, inexpensive models

Routing lets you match the model to the task rather than defaulting to your most expensive option for everything.

## Define routing rules

You can define routing rules in the admin dashboard based on:

- Request intent or keywords
- User tier or plan
- Time of day or traffic volume
- Desired cost ceiling or latency budget

```json
{
  "model": "gpt-4o-mini",
  "route": "cost-optimized"
}
```

## Fallback and reliability

The gateway can fall back to a secondary provider if the primary returns an error or hits rate limits. Configure fallback chains per model family so a single provider outage doesn't take down your application.

## Measure, then optimize

Enable usage logging and review the analytics dashboard to see which models and providers drive the most cost and latency. Route based on real data, not assumptions — then revisit your rules as new models and pricing become available.

title: Getting Started with the ZES AI Gateway
excerpt: Learn how to deploy and configure the ZES AI API gateway, connect upstream providers, and start routing requests in minutes.
content:
# Getting Started with the ZES AI Gateway

The ZES AI gateway aggregates 40+ upstream AI providers — OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, Azure, AWS Bedrock, and more — behind a single unified API. With user management, billing, rate limiting, and an admin dashboard, it's designed to be the control plane for your AI infrastructure.

## Prerequisites

Before you begin, make sure you have:

- **Node.js / Bun** installed
- A running instance of the ZES gateway (Docker is the fastest way)
- API keys for at least one upstream provider

## 1. Run the gateway

The quickest way to get started is with Docker Compose:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/zesai/zes-api.git
cd zes-api
cp .env.example .env
# Edit .env with your provider API keys
docker compose up -d
```

## 2. Configure providers

Providers are configured through the admin dashboard at `/system-settings/providers`. Add your API keys, set routing rules, and enable the models you want to expose.

## 3. Make your first request

Once the gateway is running, you can call it like any OpenAI-compatible endpoint:

```bash
curl http://localhost:3000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -d '{
    "model": "gpt-4o-mini",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello, ZES!"}]
  }'
```

## What's next

From here you can set up billing, create API keys for your team, enable rate limiting, and explore the full relay capabilities. See the [system settings](/dashboard/system-settings) guide for more.

title: Reducing AI Costs Without Sacrificing Quality
excerpt: Strategies for model routing, caching, and rate limiting that cut LLM spend while keeping response quality high.
content:
# Reducing AI Costs Without Sacrificing Quality

Large language model usage can become expensive quickly, especially at scale. The ZES gateway includes several built-in mechanisms to help you control spend without degrading the user experience.

## Smart model routing

Not every request needs your most capable (and most expensive) model. Route simple tasks — classification, extraction, short summaries — to smaller, cheaper models, and reserve flagship models for complex reasoning.

You can define routing rules in the gateway based on:

- Request intent or keywords
- User tier or plan
- Time of day or traffic volume

```json
{
  "model": "gpt-4o-mini",
  "route": "cost-optimized"
}
```

## Response caching

Cache repeated completions so identical prompts don't hit the upstream provider twice. The gateway supports semantic and exact-match caching with configurable TTLs.

## Rate limiting

Per-user and per-key rate limits prevent runaway consumption from a single client. Combine these with quotas and alerts to stay ahead of surprise bills.

## Measure, then optimize

Enable usage logging and review the analytics dashboard to see which models and users drive the most cost. Optimize based on real data, not assumptions.
